blocks.label: About {{agent.first}}
blocks.title: She grew up inside this business.
blocks.lede: Most agents learn negotiation on the job. {{agent.first}} learned it at the dinner table.
paragraphs: {{agent.first}} thrives on helping others discover the lifestyle she and her family love in Steamboat Springs. An outdoor enthusiast at heart, she takes what the Yampa Valley offers — snowboarding with her kids, hiking the trails, living in a working mountain community. Grateful to raise her children here, she understands how particular a place it is to call home.

Real estate is more than a career — it is a family legacy. With her father a respected Denver broker of more than twenty years, and her mother recognised among the top mortgage brokers in the nation, {{agent.first}} grew up immersed in the industry. That background shaped her instincts, her negotiation and her commitment to clients.

Since 2016 she has closed over 160 transactions representing $120 million in sales volume. Selling more than $15 million annually for the past five years, she ranks among the top 40 producing agents in Routt County. Her colleagues also elected her to serve on the Advisory Board at The Group Real Estate in Steamboat.

Clients describe her as approachable, professional and deeply invested in their success. Whether the search is for a primary home, a mountain retreat or an investment property, she brings the outdoor life, the family expertise and an outgoing, level temperament to every step of it.

paragraphs: Routt County is eleven submarkets pretending to be one. A buyer who reads the county median and shops on it will end up in the wrong place at the right price — or the right place two years too late. Most of {{agent.first}}'s work is spent on the question that comes before the house: which of the eleven is actually yours.

The rest is the part her clients name in reviews. She opens with a straight thirty-minute conversation about use, budget and expectations, then owns the conversations with the other side so her clients do not have to.

blocks.label: Page header
blocks.title: Eleven submarkets pretending to be one.
blocks.lede: The county-wide median is an average of places that behave nothing alike. Choosing the right one of these eleven matters more than anything you will do afterwards.

items.name: Mountain Area
items.blurb: Ski-in condominiums and lodges at the base of Mount Werner. The most rentable inventory in the valley, and the most sensitive to what the resort does next.

items.name: Downtown
items.blurb: Old Town grid, Lincoln Avenue, the Yampa River. Walkable, tightly held, and the one part of Steamboat where a lot still trades on its address alone.

items.name: Fish Creek
items.blurb: Three price points on one road. A two-bedroom condo asking $595,000 sits inside the same neighbourhood boundary as a fourteen-acre estate — so the “Fish Creek average” describes nothing.

items.name: West Steamboat & Elk River
items.blurb: Where the median dollar buys the most square footage, the biggest yard and the shortest walk to a public school. True, and the part every out-of-market buyer already knows.

items.name: Strawberry Park
items.blurb: Up the valley behind town: larger parcels, the hot springs road, and in-district school addresses without a subdivision feel.

items.name: South Valley
items.blurb: Elbow room and views eleven miles out, in the Steamboat school district. Buying acreage here is not buying a house in town — land, access, utilities and zoning shape it as much as the building.

items.name: Stagecoach
items.blurb: Twenty minutes south past the reservoir. Newer builds at Young's Peak, lots you can still buy outright, and covenants worth reading before you commit.

items.name: Oak Creek
items.blurb: A real town with a real main street, and the value end of the county that still has inventory. Where a good share of {{agent.first}}'s closings happen.

items.name: Hayden
items.blurb: The airport, new subdivisions, and the best commute-to-price ratio in the valley. The growth story most Steamboat buyers discover second.

items.name: North Routt
items.blurb: Clark, Steamboat Lake and Hahn's Peak. Trades on privacy rather than proximity; winter access is the first question, not the last.

items.name: South Routt
items.blurb: Yampa and Phippsburg — ranching country, older houses on generous lots, and a summer that now runs in a loop between the two towns.

pages.title: Buying in Routt County — Ashley Walcher's Buyer Guide
pages.desc: How Ashley Walcher works with buyers in Steamboat Springs and Routt County: four steps, starting with which of eleven submarkets is actually yours.

blocks.label: Page header
blocks.title: Buying here, in four steps.
blocks.lede: Most buyer guides run to ten steps because they are describing paperwork. This one describes the four decisions that actually change the outcome.

blocks.label: The Four Steps
blocks.title: Four decisions, in order.
blocks.lede: The Group's full buyer process sits behind this — escrow, inspection, appraisal, closing. These are the parts where you and {{agent.first}} do the thinking.

steps.title: Take the thirty-minute call first
steps.body: Before any showings: what you are looking for, how you will actually use it, what it will cost to hold, and what you are willing to trade. Clients name this call in their reviews more than anything else {{agent.first}} does, because everything downstream gets faster once it has happened.

steps.title: Pick the submarket, then the house
steps.body: Mountain Area, Downtown, Fish Creek, West Steamboat, Strawberry Park, South Valley, Stagecoach, Oak Creek, Hayden, North Routt, South Routt. Eleven different trades between price, commute, rentability and school district. Shopping across all of them at once is the most common way buyers lose a season.

steps.title: Decide your number, not your approval
steps.body: A lender will pre-approve you for more than you want to spend. Set the monthly payment you are comfortable with, then get pre-qualified against it — and budget the things a Front Range buyer forgets: plowing, propane, HOA dues that in some complexes carry the water tap, and a rental licence that may or may not transfer.

steps.title: Write an offer the seller believes will close
steps.body: Price is one term of several. Inspection window, financing contingency, closing date, post-closing occupancy, what stays with the house. {{agent.first}} owns the conversations with the other agent so you are not negotiating against your own listing agent's read of you.

pages.title: Selling in Routt County — Ashley Walcher's Seller Guide
pages.desc: How Ashley Walcher prices, prepares and markets a Steamboat Springs or Routt County property, and what the first three weeks on market decide.

blocks.label: Page header
blocks.title: Selling here, in four steps.
blocks.lede: One of {{agent.first}}'s sellers had buyers demand an abbreviated transfer timeline and still closed clean. That is what the preparation is for.

steps.title: Be honest about why you are selling
steps.body: Speed and price are different goals needing different strategies. A seller who has to be out by October is priced differently from one who wants a number. Tell {{agent.first}} which one you actually care about — pretending otherwise costs both.

steps.title: Price against your submarket, not the county
steps.body: The Routt County median is an average of eleven places that behave nothing alike, and the portals price off the aggregate. {{agent.first}} will show you the comparable closings inside your own submarket, and be direct if the number you want is not in them.

steps.title: Prepare only what returns money
steps.body: Declutter, depersonalise, fix the small broken things, deep clean. Beyond that the list is short and specific to your property — and for a rental unit it includes the occupancy history and licence paperwork a buyer's lender will ask for anyway.

steps.title: Spend the marketing in the first three weeks
steps.body: Photography, video, the MLS write-up, agent-to-agent outreach, targeted social, and the short list of buyers already looking for exactly this. Front-load it. A listing still getting first impressions in month three has usually already lost.

blocks.label: Home Valuation
blocks.title: Start with a number you can trust.
blocks.lede: Before any of the four steps you need a realistic value. An automated estimate is fine as an anchor and useless as a strategy.

pages.title: What Is My Steamboat Home Worth? — Ashley Walcher
pages.desc: Free home valuation for Steamboat Springs and Routt County property from Ashley Walcher, The Group Real Estate.

blocks.label: Page header
blocks.title: How much is your home worth?
blocks.lede: You can have the automated number in thirty seconds. It is worth what it costs, which is why {{agent.first}} sends a second one behind it.

blocks.label: How I Price
blocks.title: The median is not your price.
blocks.lede: Everything {{agent.first}} writes in the journal is really about this one problem.
paragraphs: Automated valuation models are built on volume and they price off aggregates. Routt County does not cooperate. Fish Creek alone holds a $595,000 condo and a fourteen-acre estate inside one boundary; West Steamboat leads the county on dollars-per-square-foot while trailing it on appreciation. An algorithm reading “Steamboat Springs, CO 80487” cannot see any of that.

What moves a real number here: which three sales a buyer's agent will actually use as comparables, whether a short-term rental licence transfers and what the occupancy history shows, whether the addition was permitted, what the HOA dues include, and — on acreage — access, water and buildable envelope.
So the estimate arrives first, and then a conversation. If the honest answer is that this is a bad year to sell your particular property, you will hear that too.

blocks.title: Two numbers and a plan.
